svg.title: The seven tenets of Zero Trust defined in NIST SP 800-207
svg.desc: Seven numbered rows reproducing the tenets from NIST SP 800-207 section 2.1: all data sources and computing services are resources; all communication is secured regardless of network location; access to individual resources is granted per session; access is determined by dynamic policy including observable client, application, and asset state; the enterprise monitors and measures the integrity and security posture of all owned and associated assets; all resource authentication and authorization are dynamic and strictly enforced before access is allowed; and the enterprise collects information about the current state of assets, infrastructure, and communications to improve its security posture. A footer records that SP 800-207 calls the tenets an ideal goal that may not be fully implemented in a given deployment, and that the shorter verify explicitly, least privilege, assume breach formulation is Microsoft's rather than NIST's.
svg.text: The seven tenets of NIST SP 800-207
Section 2.1 of the publication. Guidance, not a mandate — the document calls these the ideal goal.
All data sources and computing services are considered resources.
Endpoints, SaaS, small-footprint devices, and personally owned devices reaching enterprise resources all count.
All communication is secured regardless of network location.
Being inside a legacy perimeter earns nothing: the same requirements apply as from any non-enterprise network.
Access to individual enterprise resources is granted on a per-session basis.
Authorization to one resource does not automatically grant access to another.
Access is determined by dynamic policy, including observable client, application, and asset state.
May also include behavioral and environmental attributes such as usage deviation, location, and time.
The enterprise monitors and measures the integrity and security posture of all owned and associated assets.
No asset is inherently trusted; a subverted or unmanaged asset may be treated differently, up to denying all access.
All resource authentication and authorization are dynamic and strictly enforced before access is allowed.
A constant cycle of access, threat assessment, adaptation, and re-evaluation of trust during the session.
The enterprise collects as much information as possible about current asset, infrastructure, and communication state.
That data improves policy creation and enforcement, and supplies context for later access decisions.
The shorter verify explicitly / least privilege / assume breach formulation is Microsoft's, not NIST's — “assume breach” appears nowhere in SP 800-207.
